	3. A matrix A and its preconditioner M
== How to understand the probelm ==
In this research, we consider the problem ABx=b in a general Krylov subspace iterative method framework.

There are basically three types of numerical methods to solve a linear system problem.
However, when solving our special case, extra techniques should be considered.
In the present paper, we consider two approaches to solve a linear system of this structure.
The first approach apply numerical methods directly on the linear system Cx=b, under the condition C = AB.
The second approach consider an equivalent system Ay=b, Bx=y, leading to a two stage method first solving Ay=b, then solving Bx=y.
When corporating the first approach with numerical methods, Krylov subspace method is recommended considering the computational complexity, since in this method matrix-vector product is implemented in each step, reducing the complexity O(n^3) of matrix multiplication to O(n) when A, B are sparse. The second approach can be corporated with all three types of numerical methods.

In a same type of problem, an iterative method often converges faster when then condition number is smaller, and slower when the condition number is larger. And the convergence of the two approaches are not only relevant to the condition number of C, but also relevant to the condition number of A and B. For example, if the second approach is applied, when A has extremely large condition number, the iterative method could possibly stagnate or breakdown, forcing the iterations to stop.
